lesson_title: The Highlights Reel and the Team Photo: Partnership Financial Statements
hook_text: One statement is a movie. The other is a photo. Mix them up and the marks are gone.
clip_script: A soccer season ends and two things get made. The highlights reel — everything that happened all season. And the team photo — everyone lined up on the last day. Nobody asks the photo what the score was in March. That is exactly the two financial statements. The Statement of Comprehensive Income is the reel: FOR the year ended, the whole story of earning — sales of R2 460 000 at the top, costs pulled off scene by scene, net profit of R421 000 in the final frame. The Statement of Financial Position is the photo: ON 28 February, one frozen day — everything the business owns on one side, everyone with a claim on the other. And the photo rule: both lines must be the same height. R995 550 owned, R995 550 claimed. Always. Why keep both? Because each is blind to what the other sees. The reel cannot tell you if the business can pay next month's bills. The photo cannot tell you if the year was any good. And under every big number sits a note — the fine print with the workings — climbing to the exact figure on the face. Face for the conclusion. Note for the proof.
visual_style: A split frame: film reel spooling through the year's income lines on one side, a formal team photo assembling asset by asset on the other; two towers rising to identical heights, ledger-paper textures with school-sport colours.
pacing: Rolling montage for the reel, a sharp freeze for the photo, then a slow tower-balance reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build both statements to the last balancing rand.
